question: How to setup dynamic routes in Next.js?
answer:
To set up dynamic routes in Next.js, you can use the following approaches: 1. **Using dynamic segments**: You can define a route with a dynamic segment by using square brackets around the parameter name in your route path. For example: ```bash app/blog/[slug]/page.js ``` In this case, the `/blog/a` URL would be matched against `slug: 'a'`. 2. **Using generateStaticParams**: If you need to fetch data dynamically at build time, you can use the `generateStaticParams` function, which allows you to generate static routes for dynamic segments. ```tsx export async function generateStaticParams() { const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json()) return posts.map((post) => ({ slug: post.slug, })) } ``` This approach allows you to statically generate routes for your dynamic segments. 3. **Using server-side rendering**: Next.js also supports server-side rendering (SSR) for dynamic routes. With SSR, Next.js will render the page on the server and send it to the client. ```jsx export default async function Page({ params }) { const slug = (await params).slug return
My Post: {slug}
} ``` To set up dynamic routes for SSR, you can use the same syntax as above. To get started with dynamic routes in Next.js, make sure to check out the official documentation and examples on how to use them effectively.
